correctness.rationale: For every sample size at least two and every gap index including endpoints, the Dirichlet third mixed moment of a single gap with squared inter-order-statistic distances is computed directly. Summing exactly gives the quoted covariance with strictly positive denominator. Quadratic sign classification and Pell descent are all-size arguments, including parity and small-n boundaries. Independent exact Dirichlet monomial expansion verifies every rank through n=18, the sum-to-zero relation and Pell zero ranks through n=2000 (2402 exact checks). Finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full primary text of Royen, arxiv:0710.5749, Section 4/Theorem 3, and arxiv:0810.1572 concerns marginal variance distributions, not a ranked-gap mixed moment. Kochar 1999 and 2012 describe stochastic comparisons across parent distributions rather than fixed-sample covariance. Yao et al. 2008 describes spacing-vector likelihood-ratio/dependence ordering in its accessible abstract, which does not imply the explicit variance covariance or Pell zeros; its full text was unavailable. Result-level searches found structurally different published covariance results. The new contribution is the complete exact sign profile plus Pell classification, not classical Dirichlet moments or Pell solutions.

value.rationale: Local order-statistic gaps and global sample variance are standard distinct dispersion statistics. Their full covariance profile reveals a non-obvious sign reversal between outer and central gaps, sharp universal asymptotic transition fractions, and an infinite but sparse arithmetic classification of exact zero-covariance samples. These are natural complete rank/sample-size dependences, not a chosen arbitrary finite slice. Zero covariance is not promoted to independence.
